title: Potato Fondant
description: Potato fondant or also known in French as Pommes De Terre Fondantes is a technique used by cutting potatoes into cylinder shapes and browning the ends while slowly braising and roasting in stock and butter. There’s probably not a better potato as they become creamy inside and buttery roasted on the top. Great served with meats or most dishes as a side potato dish.
ingredients: 4 waxy oval potatoes (small baking or Russet potatoes, or larger “ovalish” red potatoes)
8 sprigs of fresh thyme (or 1 tsp dried)
directions: Cut off ends of potatoes, stand potatoes on end, then using a sharp paring knife, cut off the skin from top to bottom shaping it into a uniform barrel. Then cut in half and trim the larger edge into bevel shape.
Rinse potatoes in cold water to wash off any starches. Preheat your oven to 430°F – 220°C.

Place an oven proof frying pan on medium to high heat with olive oil and butter. Once melted add the potatoes bevel side down. Season with salt and pepper. Add the thyme and garlic in the hot fat around the potatoes. Cook until brown, check so they don’t burn.
Once potatoes are brown, turn them over and brown other side. Then add the chicken stock and bring to the boil. As soon as the stock boils, place in the oven at 430°F – 220°C for 30 minutes.
Most of the stock should be evaporated by the time they are cooked. Check with a knife by piercing them to be sure.
If you have juices left over, reduce them on the stove and spoon over potatoes before serving.
